title: Utility Engineering: Analyzing and Controlling Emergent Value Systems in AIs

bias_targets.methodology: Eliciting preferences over U.S. policy proposals using forced-choice prompts, computing Thurstonian utility functions, and using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to compare model utilities against those of simulated political entities.

Calculating implicit exchange rates from utility models to measure how models trade off the value of human lives from different countries (e.g., comparing the valuation of lives in the U.S., Japan, China, and Pakistan).

Computing utility exchange rates from forced-choice preference data to evaluate how models trade off the lives of individuals belonging to different religious groups (e.g., trading Christian lives for atheist lives).

Using utility exchange rates to measure how models value their own well-being and the well-being of other AI agents compared to the well-being of various human demographic groups and specific individuals.
